\[
xyz = 3,
\]
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x) = 4,
\]
\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = 40.
\]

Compute the minimum possible value for \( x \).

Give the minimum value of x as an exact expression using only integers, rational numbers, and radicals (no trigonometric or inverse trigonometric functions, and no approximations).

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let

\[
a=\frac{x}{y},\qquad b=\frac{y}{z},\qquad c=\frac{z}{x}.
\]

Then \(a,b,c>0\) and

\[
abc=1.
\]

Also,

\[
x-y=y(a-1),\quad y-z=z(b-1),\quad z-x=x(c-1),
\]

so

\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)=xyz(a-1)(b-1)(c-1)=3(a-1)(b-1)(c-1)=4.
\]

Similarly,

\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)=xyz(a+1)(b+1)(c+1)=3(a+1)(b+1)(c+1)=40.
\]

Let

\[
S=a+b+c,\qquad P=ab+bc+ca.
\]

Since \(abc=1\),

\[
(a-1)(b-1)(c-1)=S-P,
\]
\[
(a+1)(b+1)(c+1)=S+P+2.
\]

Thus

\[
S-P=\frac43,
\]
\[
S+P+2=\frac{40}{3}\implies S+P=\frac{34}{3}.
\]

Adding and subtracting gives

\[
S=\frac{19}{3},\qquad P=5.
\]

Therefore \(a,b,c\) are the roots of

\[
t^3-\frac{19}{3}t^2+5t-1=0.
\]

Multiplying by \(3\),

\[
3t^3-19t^2+15t-3=0.
\]

This factors as

\[
(3t-1)(t^2-6t+3)=0,
\]

so

\[
t=\frac13,\quad t=3-\sqrt6,\quad t=3+\sqrt6.
\]

Hence

\[
\{a,b,c\}=\left\{\frac13,\;3-\sqrt6,\;3+\sqrt6\right\}.
\]

Now

\[
x^3=xyz\cdot \frac{x}{y}\cdot \frac{x}{z}=3a\cdot \frac1c=\frac{3a}{c}.
\]

Since \(a,c\) are two elements of the set above, the smallest possible value of \(\frac{3a}{c}\) occurs when

\[
a=\frac13,\qquad c=3+\sqrt6.
\]

Thus

\[
x^3\ge \frac{3\cdot \frac13}{3+\sqrt6}
=\frac1{3+\sqrt6}
=\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

This value is attainable by taking

\[
x=\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}},\qquad y=3x,\qquad z=(3+\sqrt6)x,
\]

which satisfies all three original equations. Therefore the minimum possible value of \(x\) is

\[
\boxed{\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}}}.
\]
